artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

The SJC denied the complaint by a 20-2 vote, with a dissent disputing the majority's treatment of the complainant's constitutional and procedural claims.

artifacts.synopsis: Mrs. Sandra Lovelace complained against Northeast Presbytery's decision not to proceed to trial against teaching and ruling elders, and its ruling that her subsequent complaints were out of order due to non-membership. The SJC (reversing the Judicial Panel) denied the first item but sustained the second, holding that jurisdiction properly invoked is not forfeited by a subsequent change in the complainant's membership status.

artifacts.synopsis: Frank J. Smith complained against Northeast Presbytery after Grace Presbyterian Church was dissolved and its members were placed under Presbytery's care. The SJC ruled the complaint in order, sustained it, and returned the matter to Presbytery for adjudication, holding that dissolution did not eliminate Presbytery's pastoral responsibility or Smith's standing in the pending case.

artifacts.title: Membership status and session authority upon dissolution of a congregation

matches.evidence: Upon dissolution of a congregation, the session terminates, membership in the visible church is dissolved for those not transferred, and Presbytery may not unilaterally assign members to other churches.

artifacts.title: Mandatory prior notice requirement for congregational withdrawal from PCA

matches.evidence: A proposed notice requirement for withdrawal conflicted with BCO 25-11, which allows a church to withdraw at any time for reasons it deems sufficient.
